name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean makes a Democratic win nearly impossible
Crawford's overwhelming cash advantage: about $1.0 million on hand versus $12,000 for Green
No polls or expert ratings show any incumbent vulnerability
Prediction markets price Crawford at roughly 98 percent to win
model.rationale: The seat's R+23 lean, Crawford's incumbency, and his roughly 80-to-1 cash advantage over Terri Green leave no realistic path for an upset, and prediction markets price the race at about 98 percent Republican. The Libertarian on the ballot may trim the margin slightly but not the outcome.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal or an unprecedented anti-Republican wave would put this seat in doubt; otherwise the only open question is the size of Crawford's winning margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arkansas's first district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and Rick Crawford has held it since 2011. He enters the general election with about $1 million on hand after raising roughly $944,000, while Democratic nominee Terri Green has raised about $65,000 and had under $13,000 in the bank at last filing. A Libertarian, Steve Parsons, is also on the ballot. No public polls have surveyed the race and no expert raters have listed it, but prediction markets give Crawford roughly a 98 percent chance of winning.

The national political environment leans toward Democrats this cycle, but a swing of that size would not come close to closing a district that favors Republicans by more than twenty points in a normal year. Barring something unforeseen, Crawford is positioned for an easy re-election, with the main open question being the size of his winning margin rather than the outcome.
